_comment: Gzipped bytes. Rule 11: nothing merges over the size budget. Raising a number here is a decision, not a formality — say why in the commit. Lowering one because the measurement got more honest is a decision too: see _rederived.
_shell: Everything a visitor downloads before choosing a game: the scripts every non-play route loads eagerly, from the build's own manifests. Does not grow when a game is added, so it is the number worth defending. Deferring work off this path into an async chunk now lowers it.
_legacyPolyfills: Gzipped bytes of `polyfills-*.js`, which Next emits and references as `<script nomodule>`. Not part of the shell, because no engine `docs/support-matrix.md` supports fetches it — see `_rederived_2026_09_08_polyfills`. Budgeted anyway: we do not write this file, a Next upgrade can change it, and a bucket with no ceiling is where bytes go to hide. 40960 against 39373 measured is about 1.5 KB of room, which is enough for a patch release and not enough for a new polyfill nobody discussed.
_rederived_2026_09_08_polyfills: shellBytes 167936 -> 132096, AND THE SHELL DID NOT SHRINK BY 35 KB — the number stopped counting 38.5 KB that nobody supported ever downloads. `polyfillFiles` sits in the same manifest array as `rootMainFiles`, so `check-size.mjs` billed `polyfills-*.js` to the line described as "paid by every visitor". It is emitted as `<script nomodule>`: every engine that understands `<script type=module>` skips it without a request, and that is every engine in tiers 1 and 2 of `docs/support-matrix.md`. The only engines that fetch it are the ones that document names as tier 3 — "Internet Explorer, legacy EdgeHTML, UC Browser", not tested and not designed for. So 23% of the number rule 11 defends was fiction, and it is the same mistake #2516 fixed for the 94.9 KB of pages-router surface in the bucket four lines below it. MEASURED on this branch: 167899 total, of which 39373 is the polyfill file and 128526 is what a supported browser actually downloads. THIS DOES CREATE HEADROOM AND THAT SHOULD BE SAID PLAINLY: 132096 leaves 3570 B over the true figure where the old number left 37 B over a false one, and the batch this landed in needed about 300 of them. The headroom was always there; the metric was hiding it. Two things stop that being a loophole. The polyfills keep a budget of their own (`legacyPolyfillBytes`) rather than an exemption, because the file is Next's and a framework upgrade that doubles it should be argued about. And the exclusion is checked rather than assumed: `check-size.mjs` reads every exported page and fails the build if a polyfill script is ever referenced without `nomodule`, because at that moment everybody fetches it and it is shell again. Watched failing both ways — the attribute stripped from the export, and the file dropped from the manifest. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT #4, which asked for an initial JS payload under 150 KB gzipped excluding any game: it is met, at 125.5 KB, and has been for some time behind a number that read 164.
_rederived_2026_09_12_i18n: shellBytes 132096 -> 133230 (130.1 KB; measured 132374, 856 B headroom). The i18n framework (#219, with the `dir` half of #222 and the pseudo-locale #223 measures against). MEASURED on this branch against main de870ba built from a clean checkout on the same machine with these same scripts: main is shell 131240 / on demand 61065 / speculated 494982; this branch is 132374 / 61067 / 505829. So the whole change is +1134 B on the shell, +2 B on demand, and +10847 B speculated (explained under `_raised_2026_09_12_speculated`). WHAT THE 1134 B BUY, all of it in code every non-play route loads: `LocaleProvider` and its context (one provider in the root layout, so the header's mute, the settings page and the match HUD read one catalogue and a chosen language is fetched once), `<T>` for server components, `t()` and its `{placeholder}` fill, the locale registry with `applyLocale` stamping `lang` and `dir`, `loadCatalogue` with its two `import()` sites (which is where webpack's async-chunk boilerplate goes), `useSettings` moved to `lib/use-settings.ts`, and the language control on /settings/ with its note. `plural()` is exported and unused by any component and is shaken out; the pseudo-locale transforms and the extractor run on the build machine only and are in no chunk. WHY THE HEADROOM IS 856 B AND NOT A ROUND NUMBER: the brief for this work asked for measured plus exactly the headroom main had (132096 - 131240), so that the raise buys the framework and nothing else — the first `_raised` note to say a number inside the CI gap is a coin toss still applies, and the next change to a non-play route arrives with the same argument to make that this one had. THE KEY DESIGN IS A BUDGET DECISION and belongs here: a message id is the English string itself (`t(messages, 'Mute sound')`), not a dotted key with an English table behind it, because a table would ship every string twice — once as the id at the call site and once in the table — for a few KB gzipped across the site's copy on exactly this line, and there was less than a kilobyte to spend. The pilot in a sibling worktree measured the other design; this one ships the wrapper only. NOT IN THIS NUMBER: the catalogues. Each is an async chunk and has a bucket of its own (`localeBytes`, below), and English has none — a visitor who never opens the language control fetches no catalogue at all. WATCHED, AND WHAT DID AND DID NOT FIRE: a static `import` of a catalogue in `use-messages.ts` folds it into the shell, and the shell then measures 133181 B (130.1 KB) against this 133230 B budget — 49 B under, so THIS LINE STAYS GREEN on that fold: today's six strings fit inside the 856 B of headroom. The first draft of this note wrote the same run up as '133.2 KB against 130.1', which was the byte count read as decimal kilobytes and set against a KiB budget — a pass presented as a failure — and a review that re-ran the mutation caught it. What catches the fold is the locale-chunk check in `check-size.mjs`, which fails the build with `carries the en-XA catalogue and is in the shell`, and the lazy guard in `i18n.test.ts`, which names the importing file; both were watched failing on that same mutation. A catalogue larger than the headroom would trip this line as well, and a real translation of the whole string set is far larger than 856 B (`_locale`).
_rederived_2026_09_12_extraction: shellBytes 135630 -> 134207 (131.1 KB; measured 133351, plus the same 856 B of headroom `_rederived_2026_09_12_i18n` kept) and localeBytes 49152 -> 83968 (82.0 KB; measured 67125 for en-XA and 54140 for ar-XB, 884 strings each, about 25% over the larger). #220, the extraction, integrated: the five territories (settings, match, host, catalogue, prose) merged with each other and with main, extracted once, and measured once. THIS REPLACES the provisional notes `_raised_2026_09_12_i18n_prose_shell` (135630) and `_raised_2026_09_12_i18n_prose_locale` (49152), each measured on one territory alone and saying so. MEASURED on this branch after origin/main 4751b32 (the fonts and RTL work) was merged, built on the same machine as `_rederived_2026_09_12_i18n`: shell 132374 -> 133351, on demand 61067 -> 61832, speculated 505829 -> 511228, largest locale 929 -> 67125. WHAT THE 977 B OF SHELL BOUGHT: every user-facing string in every .tsx under apps/web/src goes through t() or <T>, and `no-untranslated-text` is now the rule for that glob rather than a ratchet — 884 msgids, of which some five hundred are data strings registered in lib/i18n/sources.ts (the game rules and controls, category names, round lengths, landing and hub copy, the settings import names and refusals, the match-options labels and refusal reasons, the offline bar, the bot tiers, the health words). The shell bytes are therefore the wrappers, not the strings: `useMessages()` and `t(messages, …)` in every client component that had a literal (header, footer, catalogue browser, cards, tiles, settings panel, key boxes, install offer, HUD, overlay, track, lobby, controls legend, every play-route panel), the `<T>` client reference for every server component that renders copy (landing, catalogue, hubs, the six prose pages, the game pages, not-found, offline), and the catalogue threaded as a parameter through the two sentence builders, seatNamesFor and gamepadNotice. The prose territory measured 134774 on its own — 1423 B MORE than the whole extraction measures here — because webpack settled its split differently once every route imports the i18n modules and the per-route copies of T.tsx that note counted are shared again; that is the reason this was re-derived once from the merge rather than summed from five raises. NOT RAISED: onDemandBytes stays 62464 against 61832 measured (+765 B, the match territory: t() in the overlay, HUD and track, the bot mark and the controller notices; 632 B of room left) and speculatedBytes stays 522240 against 511228 (+5399 B over 108 payloads, about 50 B each, which is the play route's server-rendered copy — its hidden heading and the loading line — becoming <T> elements in every payload; the host territory's commit says why that is paid; 11012 B of room, about one payload). Neither was measured item by item; both are inside their budgets. WHY LOCALE IS +25% AND NOT +856: this is one async chunk fetched by a player who chose that language, and a pseudo-locale is its worst case — en-XA doubles every ASCII byte — so a reviewed translation (#221) of the same 884 keys is expected to land under this line; the room is for strings the next batches add before #221 re-measures, not for a feature. THE SHELL LINE STILL OVER-COUNTS: check-size takes the union of every non-play route's eager scripts, so a chunk only one route loads lands on the line described as paid by every visitor (the prose note said so first); left as it is, because a more honest metric is a change to the guard, not to this number.
_measured_2026_09_12_expansion: localeBytes 83968 (82.0 KB) HELD, NOT RAISED. #223 changed the `en-XA` padding from 35% to 50% of the source length, because the acceptance criterion of that issue is a layout that survives 150% of the English and 35% is the typical case rather than the one under test. Re-measured on the same machine as `_rederived_2026_09_12_extraction`, same 867 strings: en-XA 66950 -> 68170 gzipped (+1220 B, 66.6 KB), ar-XB unchanged at 53988 because the mirror transform adds no characters. The padding is a run of one repeated middle dot per string, which is why half again the characters costs 1.8% of the bytes: gzip prices a run at close to nothing, and the raw chunk grew 261247 -> 281527. 15798 B of room left under the line. THE PSEUDO-LOCALE IS THIS BUCKET'S WORST CASE BY DESIGN — it carries the English keys and an accented, padded copy of every one of them, and the padding is now deliberately the largest expansion the layout is asked to survive rather than the one a translation is likely to bring. A reviewed translation (#221) of the same keys is expected to land further under this line than before, not nearer it.
_locale: The largest catalogue chunk, gzipped — the language a player chose, one at a time, like a game. Each non-default locale in `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/locales.ts` is reached by one `import()` in `load.ts` and is its own async chunk; `check-size.mjs` recognises it by the `locale:"…",messages:` marker every catalogue module opens with, prints one line per locale, takes it out of the on-demand total, and fails the build on a chunk naming two locales or an unregistered one, a registered locale with no chunk or two, a locale chunk folded into the shell, and an export with no locale chunk at all. English has no chunk by design — the English string is the key at every call site, so the default locale is the fallback and costs nothing. A locale chunk carries the English it translates as well as the translation, which is inherent to keying on the source string and is the reason a real locale will weigh more than the bare translation.
_set_2026_09_12_locale: localeBytes 4096 (4.0 KB; measured 929 for en-XA and 674 for ar-XB, six strings each). A NUMBER THIS FILE NEVER HAD, set for the two pseudo-locales that exist today and NOT for the site translated. What is in the chunks now is the mute labels, the language control's label and note, and the settings page's heading and lede — the strings this batch converted and nothing else, because #220 extracts the rest by file territory after this lands. 4 KB is room for the next conversions to land without an argument about this line every time, and it is deliberately far under what a full extraction will measure: every JSX text and user-facing attribute literal under apps/web/src, run through the en-XA transform and gzipped, is about 10.7 KB today (293 strings, a proxy measured with the TypeScript compiler API, not the extractor), and that is before the 108 game rules and the category copy in `data/` are registered as dynamic sources. #220 RE-DERIVES THIS from a measured full extraction rather than inheriting it; a reviewed translation (#221) is expected to weigh roughly what a pseudo-locale of the same set does, because the keys are the same English either way.
_raised_2026_09_08_service_worker: shellBytes 166912 -> 167936 (164 KB). The service worker (#192, #193, #194, #2445, #2544) is the first thing in a long while that genuinely cannot be done without new client JavaScript in the shell: a worker is registered by a script on the page, and there is no server-rendered way to do it. MEASURED, both trees built from a clean checkout with these same scripts: main a0d2cd8 is shell 165306 / on demand 47311; this branch is 166825 / 47310. So the whole change costs 1519 B on the shell and takes one byte off on demand. That buys: registration, the update prompt that lets a cached shell ever be fixed (#194), the offline indicator, and the catalogue annotation that says which games are actually on the device (#193). WHY THE RAISE IS 1024 B AND NOT THE 87 B THAT WOULD HAVE FITTED: it did fit locally — 166825 against 166912 — and CI still failed at 163.1 KB against the 163.0 KB budget. The gap between the two machines is about 190 B on the same commit, not the byte or two the note of 2026-09-08 records for two builds of one tree, because this is a different platform and a different minifier run rather than a rerun. A budget with 87 B of headroom is therefore not a budget, it is a coin toss, and the previous number had been sitting on that much slack for a while. 164 KB leaves ~1100 B over what CI actually measured, which is enough to absorb that platform difference and nothing like enough to hide a feature. NOT RAISED: onDemandBytes stays 48128 against a measured 47310, and gameChunkBytes and speculatedBytes are untouched. The worker itself is NOT in this number — `sw.js` is 8.7 KB and is now weighed on its own line by `check-size.mjs`, because no page's import graph reaches it: the page hands its URL to `navigator.serviceWorker.register` and the browser fetches it. Before that line existed it fell into "emitted and never fetched", which is the bucket that would have hidden it.
_onDemand: Everything else a player can pull that is not one game's own chunk: the play route's own scripts, plus anything reached by an import(). Nobody downloads it by arriving. Budgeted so that deferring is neither punished (it used to raise the shell) nor free.
_raised_2026_09_08_attract: onDemandBytes 58368 -> 60416 (59 KB; measured 58528 on the merge with the share card, the gamepad and the adaptive-quality work, 1888 B headroom). #165's attract stage: its own chunk is on demand by construction — it arrives through `import()` twenty seconds into an idle catalogue and never before — and it shares the engine, the registry and the bot tiers with the play route, so webpack re-cut the graph and the line moved by more than the stage weighs. Shell 130756 against 132096, +673 B for the timer, the listeners and the mount; speculated 495186, the re-cut graph spelled into 108 payloads. One measured number per merge: #2568 (solo) lands after this and re-measures.
_raised_2026_09_08_share_card: onDemandBytes 52224 -> 56320 (55 KB; measured 53891 on this branch, 2429 B headroom). #164, the share card, and #161's name filter that belongs with it. WHERE THE BYTES ARE: `lib/share-card.ts` is reached by `import()` on the first press of Share and not before — the SoundToggle -> lib/audio precedent — so it is its own async chunk, 2056 B gzipped, that a pair who never share never fetch. That is still on demand by this file's definition (anything reached by an import() from the play route), and it should be: the guard is a ceiling on what a visitor who chose a game can be asked for, and this is something they can be asked for. The rest is the button and its status line in MatchOverlay, and `containsBlockedWord` in the SDK's player-text module, which the play route already ships. MEASURED against a clean build of main in a sibling worktree, same scripts: main is shell 129963 / on demand 51113; this branch is 129981 / 53891. So the whole change is 18 B on the shell — the SDK's word list is tree-shaken out of /settings/, which imports MAX_NAME_LENGTH from the same module — and 2778 B on demand: 2056 B of async chunk, and about 720 B of button, status line and the slug prop in the play chunk. What was NOT done: the blocklist is short by design — slurs and the words that get a picture taken down, and deliberately not dick, cock or ass, which are surnames — and it is English; a name in another script is not filtered, and the module says so rather than pretending otherwise. 55 KB rather than 54 because 54 left 1405 B and CI measures 150-250 B higher than a local mac build on the same commit.
_raised_2026_09_08_batch_9: onDemandBytes 48128 -> 49152 (48 KB; measured 48563, 589 B headroom). shellBytes NOT raised and barely moved: 165310 against main a0d2cd8's 165306, four bytes, which is the point — none of this batch reaches the route every visitor lands on. The whole 1252 B is on the play route, paid by a player who has chosen a game, and it is three issues' worth: #101, canvas context loss and restoration — a 2D context is dropped under memory pressure on a phone exactly as a WebGL one is, and nothing handled it, so a reclaimed canvas left both players looking at an empty rectangle with the simulation still stepping behind it. The concrete bug inside it: `resize()` early-returns unless a measurement changed, and after a restore none has, so the DPR transform applied once at resize would never have been re-applied — the canvas comes back and every frame after draws at 1/dpr into the corner of a full-size backing store. #2424, prompts that follow the input the player actually used. `lib/input-method.ts` already existed, tagged with this issue, and was imported by nothing; its flicker defence was one rule that asserted the method switches on every alternation, which is the strobe rather than a defence against it. #1886, orientation. `orientation` has been in the manifest schema since the first game and is set by all 108, and was read by nothing. WHAT WAS NOT SPENT: `GameCard` and the catalogue are untouched, the landing page's import graph is unchanged (`lib/landing.test.ts` still passes), and Pool's new layout module is in Pool's own game chunk rather than here. 589 B of headroom is about ten times the platform variance measured on the shell between this machine and CI (189 B on a 167 KB number), so it is thin on purpose: this line is the one that grows quietly, and the next batch should have to look at it.
_raised_2026_09_08_key_bindings: onDemandBytes 49152 -> 52224 (51 KB; measured 50443 on the merge, 1781 B headroom). MEASURED ON THE MERGE, not on the branch: batch 9 (#2547) raised this to 49152 for its own 48563, and the two changes are independent, so the number that matters is the one both are in. Of the 50443, batch 9 is about 1.9 KB and this change about 1.9 KB. 51 KB rather than 50 because 50 left 757 B and CI measures 150-250 B higher than a local mac build on the same commit — the gap _raised_2026_09_08_service_worker records, and a budget inside it is a coin toss rather than a budget. #129 and #2428: the keyboard rebinding UI, and the two lines in `GameHost` that make a rebinding reach a match. WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE AND WHAT WAS NOT: `lib/key-bindings.ts` — the store, the defaults, the reserved list, the cross-seat conflict rules — plus a full test file, written and imported by nothing; and `InputManager` taking a `bindings` option that no caller in `apps/web` passed. So a player could not rebind, and a binding written into storage by hand would not have reached a match either. WHERE THE BYTES WENT, and this is the part worth reading before spending them again: the panel reaches the store through `import()` rather than importing it, because `key-bindings.ts` imports `DEFAULT_BINDINGS`, `bindingConflicts` and `otherSeat` from `@duelbox/engine` and a top-level import measured **12.7 KB on the shell** — the engine on every non-play route, paid by every visitor, for a panel most will never open. `size-budget.json` records the same trap twice for `lib/seats.ts`. Fetched instead it is two async chunks totalling 1911 B, which land on demand, which is the budget for code a visitor asked for. The storage key moved to `lib/key-bindings-key.ts` for the same reason: naming it from `player-data.ts` and `SettingsPanel.tsx` was enough to drag the engine in on its own. The remaining ~270 B is `GameHost` reading the bindings when it builds the manager. NOT RAISED: shellBytes measured 129455 against 132096, so the shell absorbed its 929 B and keeps 2641; speculatedBytes 487125 against 491520.
_raised_2026_09_08_gamepad: onDemandBytes 52224 -> 55296 (54 KB; measured 53399 on this branch against ~50.5 KB on main, 1897 B headroom). #130, gamepad support, and what the ~1.7 KB is: `GamepadManager` and `browserGamepadSource` entering the play chunk for the first time — both had been in the engine, with tests, and imported by nothing — plus the host polling them in the fixed step, the recorder writing an `analog` event so a trace with a pad replays exactly, the pause panel's one-sentence notice and its swap button, and `lib/gamepad-notice.ts`. Every byte is on the play route and only a player who has chosen a game pays it; a keyboard-and-touch pair sees no new control, because the swap is offered only after a controller has been seen. NOT RAISED: shellBytes measured 129978 against 132096 — the play-route work moved a chunk boundary by ~300 B and the shell keeps 2118. The number is 54 KB rather than 53 because 53 would have left 873 B and CI measures 150-250 B higher than a local build on the same commit; a budget inside that gap is the coin toss this file keeps arguing against.
_raised_2026_09_08_quality: onDemandBytes 55296 -> 57344 (56 KB; measured 54644 on this branch, 2700 B headroom). #31 and #190: the adaptive-quality feed, the per-game DPR cap and the battery gate, all on the play route. WHAT THE ~1245 B OVER THE GAMEPAD BRANCH'S 53399 IS: `AdaptiveQuality` entering the play chunk for the first time — it had been in the engine, with tests, and wired to nothing — plus `RenderGate`, `isLowPower`, `browserBatterySource`, the loop's new `frame` callback and the host feeding all four. Shell 129962 against 132096, unmoved: nothing here touches a non-play route. WHY A RAISE AND NOT 652 B OF HEADROOM: CI measures 150-250 B higher than a local mac build on the same commit (the gap _raised_2026_09_08_service_worker records), so 652 B is about 450 on the machine that decides, and this file has said more than once that a budget inside the noise is a coin toss rather than a budget. 56 KB leaves about one more feature of this size before the next argument. NOT RAISED: speculatedBytes measured 490464 against 507904. RE-MEASURED ON THE MERGE with #2560 and #2561 both in: 56931, against which 57344 would have left 413 B — inside the CI noise. 58368 (57 KB) leaves 1437 B. One measured number per merge.
_raised_2026_09_08_solo: onDemandBytes 56320 -> 59392 (58 KB; measured 57678 on the tree that has #2560, #2561 and #2563 merged, 1714 B headroom). #1750: the solo score-attack mode — one seat on the play route, a one-seat scoreboard, a result screen that shows a score against this device's best, and the best-score store that reads and writes it. MEASURED AGAINST THE MERGE, NOT AGAINST MAIN: two open pull requests raised this line while this one was written (the share card to 56320, the gamepad to 55296), and the honest baseline is the tree with both in it — see the figure below: built from a clean checkout of that merge with these same scripts, it is shell 130377, on demand 56667, speculated 489767 — which means the two raises together were already 347 B over the 56320 the second of them set, before this batch added a byte. This batch is +1011 B on demand, +74 B on the shell and +215 B speculated. What the bytes buy, all of it on the play route: `PlaySurface` seating one player (single-seat presentation, the opening seat pinned to p1, the run recorded to a best rather than a head-to-head), `MatchHud` drawing one seat, `MatchOverlay`'s solo ending and its announcement, `lib/best-scores.ts`, and `offeredModes` doing the lobby's filtering. NOT RAISED: shellBytes measured 130451 against 132096, 75 B for `BEST_SCORES_KEY` reaching `player-data.ts` through its own `-key.ts` module, which is the pattern that keeps a store off the shell. The six games' solo branches are in their own chunks, which are held by gameChunkBytes and moved by tens of bytes. RE-MEASURED ON THE MERGE with the share card, the gamepad and the adaptive-quality work all in: 58689, against which 59392 would have left 703 B — inside the CI noise. 61440 (60 KB) leaves 2751 B, and the attract stage (#2569, +~700 B measured on its own merge) lands beside this; whichever of the two lands second re-measures and sets one number.
_raised_2026_09_08_download_all: onDemandBytes 62464 -> 64512 (63 KB; measured 62511 on the merge of #2572 (tournament flow) and #2568 (solo) into this branch, 2001 B headroom; first measured 53535 against 55296 before the batches it queued behind). #196, download all games. MEASURED against main at 5a9e0ac plus #2563, same scripts, same machine: shell 130367 -> 130531 (+164 B: a heading, a note and a lazy mount on /settings/), on demand 52086 -> 53535 (+1449 B: the control itself, reached through lazy() so its sentences, its progress bar and its two storage calls are paid by the person who opened the section rather than by every visitor to every route), and the service worker 8865 -> 16512 (+7647 B, on the line that has no budget and is paid once per deploy). THAT LAST NUMBER IS THE ONE TO KNOW ABOUT. About half of it is the download list — 108 slugs, 108 hashed chunk names and 108 weights, plus the play route's shared chunks listed once — and half is the code and its comments, which the worker ships verbatim because public/ is copied and not bundled. The first version of the list repeated the shared route chunks per game: the worker was 17024 and the total it offered was 6.2 MB, of which 5 MB was the same fifty kilobytes counted 108 times. Listing them once made the total honest — 1265 KB, which is what a person who presses the button downloads — and took 512 B off the worker. Why the shell moved only 164 B for a feature with a progress bar in it: everything but the heading is in components/DownloadAll.tsx behind lazy(), and the list, the fetching, the eviction and the progress live in the worker, which is the one place they cost the shell nothing. RE-MEASURED ON THE MERGE with the share card, the gamepad, the adaptive-quality work and the install prompt all in: on demand 59724, so 61440 (60 KB, the number #2568 set on its own merge) leaves 1716 B. And firstSessionBytes 327680 -> 337920 (330 KB; measured 330240): the first-session line counts the worker, and the worker grew 7.6 KB here — about half of it the 108-entry list of every game's chunk and its size, which is the thing that lets the settings page say '108 games, 1.2 MB' before a byte is fetched. Paid once per deploy, stated rather than hidden, and the line is held at 7.7 KB of headroom so the next thing that grows the worker has to say so too.
_raised_2026_09_08_tournament_flow: onDemandBytes 61440 -> 62464 (61 KB; measured 61064 on the merge of #2568 (solo) on main 9680be3 (attract), 1400 B headroom). #2347 and #2351: a tournament that plays the bot at one tier, and a match that changes between rounds without losing its score. MEASURED ON THE MERGE, as the solo and attract notes both ask: this branch alone, on the solo branch before it was rebased, was on demand 59840 against 58689 for that branch, so the work itself is +1151 B; the merge with the attract stage in is 61064 (nine of them the per-round rebuild in `GameHost` that the same e2e found wanting), which is the one number for the three of them. WHAT THE 1151 B IS, all on the play route: `lib/match-changes.ts` (the one rule for what a running match may change, with a reason on every refusal), the round result's "Change something for the next round" block in `MatchOverlay` reusing `MatchOptions` with a `lengths` filter, the hand-over and the `mixed` flag in `PlaySurface`, `difficulty` on the tournament record and store, and one line each on the track and the HUD saying the tier. NOT RAISED: shellBytes measured 131239 against 132096 — this branch adds nothing to the shell (130557 before the merge against the solo branch's 130451, a chunk boundary); the 857 B left is above the 150-250 B CI gap but is the next line to argue about. speculatedBytes 494576 against 507904. 61 KB rather than 60 because 376 B of headroom is inside the gap this file keeps calling a coin toss.
_raised_2026_09_07_overnight: onDemandBytes 41984 -> 47104 (measured 46797, ~307 B headroom); shellBytes NOT raised and measured 161.4 KB against the 163 KB allowed, so the number the guard most defends kept its headroom. What the ~4.8 KB on the play route buys, all real match-flow chrome added this session: the in-match exit control with a forfeit-confirmation dialog (#144), Restart and Settings added to the pause menu (#145), a game error boundary that catches a throw from update()/render(), stops the loop and offers recovery rather than a white screen (#151), and the pre-match countdown rendered upright per seat (#142).
